title: They say in the West
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.6) associates this expression with Rabbi Yirmeyah. Hyman interprets this to mean that Rabbi Yirmeyah, who went up from Babylonia to the Land of Israel, grew and succeeded greatly in his learning, until at the end of his days he was one of the greats of the generation and gained an established place there, such that people knew that wherever they said "in the West," it was known to them that it was from Rabbi Yirmeyah.

We find the expression "They say in the West" in [Nazir 20b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.20b.1), [Sotah 18b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.18b.8), [Bava Metzia 94b:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.94b.15), [Zevachim 89b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.89b.5), 90a, [Zevachim 91b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.91b.5), [Chullin 55b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.55b.3), [Bekhorot 13a:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.13a.12), and Arakhin 17a.[^9]

Hyman argues: As for what we find in [Berakhot 8a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.8a.15), "They say in the West: this statement of Mar Zutra is preferable to all of them" — this does not mean that Rabbi Yirmeyah heard from the words of Mar Zutra, for Mar Zutra lived after Rabbi Yirmeyah, and in his days there was no remnant or survivor of the Land of Israel's academies. Rather, Mar Sutra’s [supplied מר סוטרא] statement had already been said in the days of Rabbi Yirmeyah, and only in Babylonia was it repeated in the study hall in the name of Mar Zutra and fixed in his name.

But we also find, explicitly, the expression "They say in the West" for sayings that do not belong to Rabbi Yirmeyah, such as in [Berakhot 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.14b.4): "When Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah came, he said: they say in the West." And in [Sanhedrin 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.23a.12), "They say in the West in the name of Rabbi Zeira [supplied ר״ז]"; in [Bekhorot 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.15b.7), in the name of R' Chanina; and in [Bava Batra 80a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.80a.4) and [Chullin 32a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.32a.11), [Chullin 50b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.50b.5), [Chullin 57a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.57a.6), in the name of R' Yose bar R' Chanina.

Hyman gives [Horayot 13a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.13a.4), [Bava Batra 16b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.16b.12), Yoma 86a, and Zevachim 94a as instances in the name of Rava bar Mari. He also cites Berakhot 33b in the name of Ravina, which he says should read Ravinai. And in [Berakhot 2b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.2b.3): "In the West, this statement of Rava bar Shila was not heard by them."[^7][^8][^10]

notes.text: The abbreviation ר"ז appears in the source without expansion; no supplied registry entry resolves it, so it is left in Hebrew.
The source text prints the name as מר סוטרא in one place and מר זוטרא elsewhere in the same paragraph; this appears to be a typographical variant and is rendered as Mar Zutra.
The source itself marks "רבינא" with the correction "וצ"ל דרבינאי" (it should read Ravinai); preserved as printed.

Whole source and all notes reviewed. אמרי במערבא is a reporting formula, not a person: heading translated literally with no authority target. Hyman owns reconstruction about RabbiYirmeyah’s place, chronology, academy disappearance and reassignment of MarZutra’s saying; no independent historical proof. זכות אזרח means an established place in this argument, not independently documented citizenship rights. Source מר סוטרא is now visibly MarSutra alongside other MarZutra occurrences, without a printed-error claim. Ravinai is Hyman’s proposed correction, not silent normalization. ר״ז in San23a remains unresolved/held rather than automatically expanded. All citations/old questions retained. References to printed/native readings in inherited notes are preserved historical claims; this root pass uses supplied digital text and named saved editions, not a fresh pixel or correction-history verification.

The whole named Davidson Sanhedrin 23a paragraph explicitly writes Rabbi Zeira in this reporting formula, locally supporting the supplied ר״ז expansion. Sanhedrin 17b’s whole mnemonic paragraph explicitly names Rabbi Yirmeyah for אמרי במערבא; its following whole reversal paragraph concerns two other formulas and is not substituted for this one. These readings do not turn the formula into a person or prove Hyman’s biographical and chronological reconstruction. The p004 source hold and all four current mixed notes remain verbatim, while the newly supported local expansion is stated separately; no mixed-note retirement or authority-wide binding is made. The uncollated p004 Chanina/Yose titles remain R'. Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah is fully written in the supplied source. Mar Sutra/Mar Zutra stay distinct, and Hyman’s should-read Ravinai is retained with its full force. All other source locators, negation, emphatic claims, and the no-remnant-or-survivor argument remain Hyman’s statements; no extra legal material or primary figures are imported.

Sanhedrin 17b lists R’ Yirmeyah for this formula. The reversal in the next passage concerns two other expressions. Sanhedrin 23a spells out R’ Zeira in the formula quoted here, and Berakhot 14b has Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah transmit a Western report. These are separate occurrences of the expression. Berakhot 8a names Mar Zutra and records the Western preference for his statement. Hyman’s printed notice (I, pp. 230–231) also reads Mar Zutra where the supplied transcription has Mar Sutra. Hyman’s account of the chronology and subsequent attribution is his interpretation. At the end of the notice the print reads Rabbah bar Shila, and Davidson Berakhot 2b names Rabbah bar Rav Sheila and says his statement had not reached them in the West. The supplied form is rendered Rava bar Shila above. The print also appears to read Rabbah bar Mari in the earlier list. The examined Berakhot 33b passages include a separate exchange in which Ravina addresses Rava and a distinct Western dispute. Hyman’s proposed Ravinai remains unconfirmed.

The formula is associated with Yirmeyah in the Sanhedrin mnemonic. The other linked passages furnish distinct local attributions, including Rabbi Zeira, Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Chanina. Berakhot 2b names Rabbah bar Rav Sheila.

The consulted texts of [Horayot 13a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.13a.4) and [Bava Batra 16b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.16b.12) name Rava bar Mari and Rabbah bar Mari respectively. Where Hyman gives Yoma 86a, [Yoma 86b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.86b.5) has Rabbi Yitzchak report a Western teaching in the name of Rabbah bar Mari. On Berakhot 33b, [Berakhot 33b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.33b.1) has Ravina ask Rava about havdalah, and [Berakhot 33b:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.33b.18) names Rabbi Yose bar Avin and Rabbi Yose bar Zevida in a Western dispute. Hyman’s proposed Ravinai remains unconfirmed.

The formula stands at the end of [Arakhin 16b:24](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.16b.24); the words it introduces open [Arakhin 17a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.17a.1), the folio Hyman cites. [Arakhin 15b:21](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.15b.21) gives another use of the formula, about harmful speech.

[Zevachim 90b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.90b.6) has the Western report in Rava bar Mari’s name about the missing alef. Hyman cites Zevachim 94a. This parallels the linked Horayot passage, with Ravina in Zevachim and Rava in Horayot for the response about the ordinance.
